stem: A 30-month-old boy does not seem to notice people entering the room, rarely responds to sounds, and makes little eye contact. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Reassure the family and review in 12 months
Prioritise a structured developmental assessment with hearing and vision checks
Begin routine broad investigations before taking a history
Focus only on behaviour rating scales
Assume this is normal variation because he is under 5 years

explanation: Structured developmental assessment with hearing and vision checks is the most appropriate next step. Reduced response to social, visual, and auditory stimuli with limited eye contact are red flags, so the assessment should be systematic and include sensory evaluation early.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Red flags at all ages; Developmental Delay

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Assessment: history is critical; always check hearing and vision

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because reassurance alone ignores red-flag social, visual, and auditory concerns that need assessment.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because these features are developmental red flags and the next step is a structured assessment with hearing and vision checks.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because broad investigations are not the first step; history, examination, and targeted sensory checks come first.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because behaviour rating scales alone do not address possible developmental delay or sensory impairment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because being under 5 years does not make these findings normal; developmental concerns still require assessment.
